title: Applicability and effectiveness of passive, back-supporting exoskeletons in logistics and care - a randomized controlled trial
summary:
Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are one of the most common health problems among employees in Europe. Around 60% of employees are affected, often due to heavy physical work, repetitive movements or awkward postures. These illnesses not only lead to longer periods of absence, but also cause high costs - around 240 billion euros a year.
One possible solution is passive exoskeletons, which relieve the strain on the back and thus prevent injuries. Initial studies show positive effects, especially in the laboratory. However, there is still little knowledge about how well they help in everyday working life and whether they protect workers from MSDs in the long term.
The ELSA study is investigating whether passive back-supporting exoskeletons can effectively contribute to relieving back strain in physically demanding work areas such as logistics and care. The study not only evaluates their health effects, but also examines the challenges that arise during use and how these can be overcome. The aim is to gain sound knowledge in order to integrate exoskeletons specifically into preventive measures against musculoskeletal disorders.

interventions.name: Intervention group - receives a passive exoskeleton BionicBack (hTrius GmbH) for 3 months with follow-up appointments and asynchronous education on the use of the exoskeleton. This includes monitoring the frequency of wear

Intervention group - receives a passive exoskeleton SoftExo/CareExo Lift (HUNIC GmbH)  for 3 months with follow-up appointments and asynchronous education on the use of the exoskeleton. This includes monitoring the frequency of wear
Control group - does not receive an exoskeleton and works as usual. The data collection is identical to the IG.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Workers from the logistics or care sectors with recurring lifting tasks in their daily work routine 
- High risk potential due to lifting and carrying loads (number over 10 per working day or weight over 10 kg per lifting or carrying load)
Exclusion criteria:
- acute viral/bacterial infections and infectious diseases
- Physical, mental or other inability to provide requested information or participate in required tests (Folstein et al., 1975; Watson et al., 1993)
- Orthopaedic, rheumatologic, cardiovascular or psychiatric conditions that prevent the use of passive exoskeletons
- Pregnancy
